q1.question: How many papers in the corpus were published in 2025, and how does Reflexion use verbal self-reflection?
q1.answer_text: 19 papers in the corpus were published in 2025. [D1]Reflexion uses verbal self-reflection to improve subsequent attempts without updating model weights. Instead, it turns task feedback into natural-language lessons stored in episodic memory. [C1]Its process is:An Actor generates actions or text, and an Evaluator assesses the resulting trajectory. [C2]A Self-Reflection LLM examines the feedback—such as success/failure—alongside the trajectory and existing memory, then produces specific guidance about what went wrong and what to do differently. [C3, C4]The reflection is saved in memory; on later attempts, the Actor uses these lessons together with the current trajectory history to guide its decisions. [C4]This creates a trial–evaluate–reflect–retry loop, with memory typically limited to the most recent 1–3 reflections to fit the model’s context window. [C4, C5]
